input.summary: Affiliate sessions in FR jumped from about 500/hour to about 2,700-2,900/hour starting 10:00 on 2026-09-19, roughly 5.5x expected, while the same channel in other countries rose only modestly (DE +452/h, others under +160/h). Checkout conversion for this slice fell from about 4.5% to 1.5-1.7%, across all platforms. The planned all-country weekend sale does not explain a surge confined to one channel and country. No change-log entry covers affiliate FR, and the web-2.36.1 release and APP5 coupon do not fit. Pattern suggests bot or junk affiliate traffic, but orders roughly doubled, which argues against a pure bot explanation. Not established: the traffic source and whether orders are genuine. No mitigation proposed.

Web_mobile sessions fell about 65% from 09:00 on 2026-09-29 (1,740 to 1,960 per hour vs ~4,800-5,500 expected), while app_android, app_ios and web_desktop were flat. The only web_mobile change nearby is CHG-01828, a gtm-web container v212 publish (consent banner update) at 08:50, which fits the timing and platform. Net revenue on web_mobile stayed near expected (about 21k-23k per hour vs 23k expected at 11:00), so real orders did not fall. This points to lost session tracking, not lost traffic. I did not verify the tag's contents or the country split, and I did not check the consent banner directly. No mitigation proposed, since tracking_outage has none; the tag change should be reviewed.

Payment success rose modestly above expected from 12:00 (0.947 vs 0.924 expected) but at 13:00 it was only 0.935 vs 0.931 expected, so the alert is close to normal variation. The rise is spread across providers (psp_beta, gamma, alpha up; psp_delta flat/down) and most countries (PL down), with no single concentrated cause. Nearby changes: android-5.17.2 released 13:20 (basket badge fix), ps-de-brand campaign edits, and a FREESHIP coupon created 08:54; none is linked to a payment-success increase, and no calendar events exist. Cause not established; no mitigation proposed. Monitor whether the uplift persists.

DE wallet payment success fell from about 97% expected to 87% at 08:00 (window 05:00-09:00 at 90.2% on psp_gamma, the only provider in the slice). The drop starts around 06:00, after psp_gamma's certificate rotation on the DE wallet gateway began at 05:30 (CHG-01071, provider_status). Only one provider appears in the breakdown, so the effect is concentrated on psp_gamma. Recommended mitigation: fail over DE wallet traffic from psp_gamma. Not established: whether the rotation is the sole cause, and whether volume is affected beyond the success rate. Small hourly volumes overnight make early readings noisy.

NL web_desktop checkout_conversion fell from about 0.058 expected to 0.022-0.029 from 16:00 to 21:00 on 2026-08-14, while sessions stayed near expected. The drop is across all channels and all four payment providers' success rates are near baseline. Discount rate is normal. Change log has two entries: SOMMER15 description edit (12:57), which does not change discount rate, and a price change on one lighting SKU (LIG-84603, 19:02), which starts after the drop and is too narrow to explain it. No planned event in the calendar. Cause not established; the on-call should check the checkout funnel and desktop web releases or tracking for NL, which I could not query.

content.text: The sessions drop on web_mobile starts at 09:00, right after a tag change at 08:50. I'll check whether orders held steady and whether the drop is limited to this platform.

input.summary: Paid search sessions in ES fell from about 392-445 expected per hour to 88-102 from 08:00 on 2026-10-06. The drop is confined to paid_search in ES; other ES channels are flat or up. Change CHG-01931 (07:55) set campaign ps-es-brand-q4 to "budget exhausted", five minutes before the drop began, so the campaign likely stopped spending. No planned event explains it. Caveat: I did not verify spend data directly, and the budget status is the only campaign-side evidence. Resuming the campaign is the proposed fix if the budget should continue.

Furniture discount rate jumped from about 6% to 24% starting 08:00 on 2026-09-09 and stayed there through 10:00. The jump is the same in every country (AT, DE, ES, FR, NL, PL), so it is not a country effect. Gross margin in furniture fell from about 38% to 22-25% over the same hours. Change CHG-01532 at 07:40 changed coupon MOEBEL25 (furniture) from 5% to 25%, which fits the timing and direction. No planned event explains it. Not established: the coupon's order count and whether its redemptions are legitimate. Recommend disabling MOEBEL25 and checking margin on furniture orders placed since 08:00.

FR card payment success fell from about 0.92-0.95 expected to about 0.40 starting 10:00 UTC on 2026-10-13, and stayed there through 12:00. The breakdown shows all FR card traffic in the window on psp_beta, which dropped from 0.93 to 0.41. The change log has a status-feed entry at 09:55 for a partial outage on psp_beta card authorisations in FR, filed 5 minutes before the drop. No calendar event explains it. The unrelated android release and price update in the window do not fit a payment drop. The breakdown has no other provider to compare against, so I could not confirm alternative providers are healthy. Recommend failing FR card traffic over from psp_beta.

The alert says web_mobile sessions are below expected, but sessions are above expected. At 20:00 on 2026-09-20, web_mobile had 17,108 sessions against an expected 10,344 (about +65%). The rise started around 05:00 and has continued since. It is not limited to one slice: web_desktop, both app platforms, all six countries and all five channels rose by similar proportions over 17:00–21:00 versus the prior week. A planned all-country "Autumn weekend sale" (CAL-008, 18–21 Sept) covers this window and fits a broad rise. No change-log entry fits a web_mobile-only cause. Nothing shows conversion or payment problems, though I did not check conversion. The direction in the alert does not match the data, so the alert may be misconfigured. Confidence is medium because the sale is inferred from timing and breadth, not confirmed by its traffic effect.

NL web_desktop checkout conversion fell from about 0.05-0.06 to 0.022-0.036 from 16:00 to 18:00 (18:00 at 0.026 vs 0.068 expected). The drop is steepest on this slice (-4.0 pts vs -1.3 pts for DE and -0.6 for FR), but NL app and mobile web also fell. Sessions are normal, so bot traffic does not fit. Payment success by provider shows no clear single-provider failure, though volumes are small. No calendar event and no change-log entry for NL or desktop fits: the 06:30 tax-table config, 09:00 pixel-social tag and 12:57 SOMMER15 description edit all predate the drop or do not match it. Cause not established; the on-call should check checkout errors and NL-specific configuration directly.

Whole-business sessions are up about 3-5% since 18:00 on 13 Oct. Almost all of the excess sits in Spain paid search: about 660 sessions/hour against a baseline of 160, roughly 4x. Spain paid-search checkout conversion fell to 4.1% at 19:00 from an expected 5.5%, and net revenue in that slice is below expected, so the extra sessions are not buying. The change log has no Spain paid-search entry in the window; the only nearby paid-search change is ps-nl-shopping (NL, 19:58). The pattern fits bot traffic, but I did not confirm it from device or session-level data. Not established: the source of the traffic, and whether it is an actual bot. Mitigation is the bot challenge for ES paid_search, pending review.

Email sessions rose about 3x from 16:00 on 2026-09-10 (4832 vs 1644 expected at 16:00; 5302 vs 1734 at 17:00). This matches planned campaign CAL-007, the autumn catalogue newsletter to all countries, running 16:00-20:00. Email checkout conversion stayed in its normal range (0.065 at 16:00, 0.071 at 17:00, against expected 0.068), and the rise appears in every country, which fits a newsletter send rather than bot traffic. No change-log entry fits the timing. The spike is larger than a typical send, so the on-call may want to confirm the campaign's expected volume. No mitigation is proposed.

PL kitchen gross margin fell from ~0.42 expected to ~0.04 (window 07:00-13:00, 2026-09-23), with negative margins at 09:00-10:00. Only kitchen moved in PL (other categories flat or within noise). Change CHG-01749 at 06:45 wrote a EUR price (349.00) for KIT-22050 into the PLN price field, which would underprice that SKU and explain negative margin. Timing matches the drop. Not verified: order-volume rise and per-SKU split, since the tools do not split by SKU. Other changes (web/android search releases, campaigns) do not fit the kitchen-only margin drop. Recommend pausing KIT-22050 listing and correcting the PLN price.

Not established: the exact tag fault, and whether the drop is purely measurement. No mitigation proposed; the fix is to check and roll back the tag.
